correctness.rationale: Under probabilists Hermite normalization, He_n(x)+b He_(n-2)(x)=(-1)^m 2^m m! x^delta [L_m^{delta-1/2}(x²/2)-(b/(2m))L_(m-1)^{delta-1/2}(x²/2)] for n=2m+delta. Interlacing ensures at least m-1 positive simple Laguerre zeros. The quotient B_m(s)=2m L_m(-s)/L_(m-1)(-s) has strictly positive derivative and nonpositive second derivative by the positive-residue continued fraction; B_m(0)=n-1 even or n odd. Hence for b>threshold exactly one negative Laguerre zero gives precisely two imaginary Hermite zeros; at equality zero multiplicity 2+delta; below all simple real. Inverting B_m gives convex y²(b), increasing slope from 1/(n-1) even or 3/n odd to 1 and sharp global bounds c_n(b-b_c)<=y²<=b-b_c, with equality n=2,3 and strict n>=4.
